### ✅ Step 2A — Marriage: Bridget Gleeson × Michael O'Connor, 4 March 1924, Croom SRD

**Group ID: 1224468 — image 5312233.pdf confirmed and read.**

| Field | Bride (Bridget) | Groom (Michael) |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Bridget Gleeson | Michael O'Connor |
| Condition | Full Spinster | Full Bachelor |
| Residence | **Main Street, Croom** | Rathdrum |
| **Father's Name** | **Patrick Gleeson** | Michael J O'Connor |
| **Father's Occupation** | **Farmer** | Accountant |
| Witnesses | Michael T Bregg, Mary Foley |
| Priest | Timothy Curtins PP, Croom |
| Chapel | Church of [Mary], Croom |

**This is the single most important find of the session.** The marriage register of 1924 explicitly records Bridget's father as **"Patrick Gleeson, Farmer"** of **Main Street, Croom**. This definitively links our Patrick Gleeson (Carrier/Farmer, died 7 December 1897, Croom) to this household. The "Carrier" on the death cert vs "Farmer" on the marriage cert is a completely normal inconsistency — carriers often also farmed, and the register-filler would have used whatever was given verbally.

## What To Do Next

The single most actionable next step is now the **Margaret Moloney death cert image** (Group ID 4858114) — the informant "Ellen" on that cert is the remaining open question tying the Gleeson side to the Moloney side. Given that we now know Patrick Gleeson's address was **Main Street, Croom** and Ballinscola (Margaret Moloney's address) is just outside Croom town, the geography fits perfectly. The working hypothesis is that Ellen Moloney married into the Gleeson family or is a Gleeson by birth, and that Margaret Moloney and Margaret Gleeson are one generation apart.
